sources.excerpt: London Heathrow Airport (IATA: LHR, ICAO: EGLL) – named London Airport until 1966 – is the primary and largest international airport serving London, the capital of England and the United Kingdom.
Before the opening of CDG in 1974, Orly was the main airport of Paris.
It is located partially in and named after Orly, 13 kilometres (8 mi; 7 nmi) south of Paris.

LaGuardia Airport (IATA: LGA, ICAO: KLGA, FAA LID: LGA) is a civil airport in East Elmhurst, Queens, New York City, United States, situated on the northwestern shore of Long Island, bordering Flushing Bay.
King's Cross railway station, also known as London King's Cross, is a passenger railway terminus in the London Borough of Camden, on the edge of Central London.

Gare du Nord is the Paris terminal station of the Eurostar network and serves international destinations in Belgium, Germany, the Netherlands, and the United Kingdom as well as northern France and the northern outskirts of Paris.

Pennsylvania Station (also known as New York Penn Station or Penn Station) is the main intercity railroad station in New York City and the busiest transportation facility in the Western Hemisphere, serving more than 600,000 passengers per weekday as of 2019.
Piccadilly Circus is a road junction and public space of London's West End in the City of Westminster.
By the late 19th century, the Champs-Élysées had become a fashionable avenue; the trees on either side had grown enough to form rectangular groves (cabinets de verdure).
Paris Métro Line 1 runs under the Champs-Élysées.
Together with adjacent Duffy Square, Times Square is a bowtie-shaped plaza five blocks long between 42nd and 47th Streets.
It is formed by the junction of Broadway, Seventh Avenue, and 42nd Street in Midtown Manhattan, New York City.

editorNotes: The column is read as the city an airport serves, because none of the three sits neatly inside its city centre: Heathrow is in the London Borough of Hillingdon and LaGuardia is in Queens, within New York City, while Orly, as its own article says, lies 13 kilometres south of Paris. Both Orly sentences are given as sources so the reader can see exactly what is being claimed; Charles de Gaulle would have raised the same point, since no airport lies inside Paris proper. Several tiles have namesakes on the underground railways, and each time the tile names the surface place rather than the station: Piccadilly Circus is the junction above Piccadilly Circus tube station, Times Square is the plaza above the Times Square-42nd Street subway station, the Champs Elysees is the avenue with Metro Line 1 running beneath it, and Heathrow is the airport, not its rail stations, so none of them doubles as an answer in the railway station row. Kings Cross names the terminus in Camden rather than the surrounding district, so it stays in the station row, and Penn Station and Gare du Nord are railway stations and nothing else. Every tile satisfies exactly one cell, so the placement is forced and no two tiles can be exchanged.
